sections.title: Basic Concept of Parts of Speech
sections.content: Parts of Speech are word categories that indicate how a word functions in a sentence. Step 1: Identify the word's role in the sentence. Step 2: Check if it's a person/thing, an action, a quality, or the manner of an action. Step 3: Determine its category based on this. Main categories: Noun, Pronoun, Verb, Adjective, Adverb.

sections.title: Types of Nouns (Proper, Common, Collective, Abstract)
sections.content: Step 1: Check if the word is the name of a person, place, or thing. If yes, it is a Noun. Step 2: If it's a specific name like Ram, Delhi – Proper Noun. If it's a general name like boy, city – Common Noun. Step 3: If it denotes a group like team, army – Collective Noun. If it denotes a feeling or quality like honesty, happiness – Abstract Noun.

sections.title: Basic Usage of Pronouns (Subjective, Objective, Possessive)
sections.content: A Pronoun takes the place of a Noun. Step 1: See if the Pronoun is the Subject or Object in the sentence. I, he, she, they – Subjective case. me, him, her, them – Objective case. Step 2: If it shows ownership like my, his, their – Possessive case. Step 3: The form of the Pronoun changes according to its role.

sections.title: Difference between Adjective and Adverb
sections.content: Step 1: See what the word is describing. If it describes a Noun, it's an Adjective (good boy). Step 2: If it describes a Verb, it's an Adverb (runs well). Step 3: Adverbs often end in -ly (quickly, slowly), but not always. Understand the difference between good (Adjective) and well (Adverb).

sections.title: How to Identify an Underlined Word
sections.content: Step 1: Read the entire sentence. Step 2: What question does the underlined word answer? Who? What? How? When? Step 3: Determine the Part of Speech accordingly. Example: She runs fast. Here, fast describes runs, so it is an Adverb.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Confusion between Adjective and Adverb (good/well). 2. Wrong Pronoun case ('Me went' is wrong, 'I went' is right). 3. Not using a capital letter for a Proper Noun. 4. Treating a Collective Noun as plural.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: A Noun names. A Pronoun replaces a Noun. An Adjective describes a Noun. An Adverb describes a Verb. Identifying the role of the underlined word is the most important step.

tricks.title: Trick to Identify a Noun
tricks.explanation: Step 1: Can a, an, or the come before the word? Step 2: Is it a name? If yes, it will be a Noun.
tricks.example: The boy is playing. 'boy' is a Noun.

tricks.title: Proper Noun Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: Is the word a specific name? Step 2: Is the first letter capitalized? Then it will be a Proper Noun.
tricks.example: Delhi is a big city. 'Delhi' is a Proper Noun.

tricks.title: Pronoun Case Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: If it's before the Verb, it's Subjective (I, he). Step 2: If it's after the Verb or preposition, it's Objective (me, him).
tricks.example: She called me. Here, 'me' is Objective.

tricks.title: Identifying Possessives
tricks.explanation: Step 1: Does it show ownership? Step 2: Look for words like my, your, his, their.
tricks.example: This is my book. 'my' is a Possessive Pronoun.

tricks.title: Adjective vs Adverb Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: If it describes a Noun, it's an Adjective. Step 2: If it describes a Verb, it's an Adverb.
tricks.example: She is a good singer. (Adjective) She sings well. (Adverb)

tricks.title: -ly Identification Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: If the word ends in -ly, it will often be an Adverb. Step 2: Check whether it is describing a Verb or not.
tricks.example: He runs quickly. 'quickly' is an Adverb.

tricks.title: Collective Noun Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: Does the word show a group? Step 2: Is it used as a single unit? Then it's a Collective Noun.
tricks.example: The team is winning. 'team' is a Collective Noun.

tricks.title: Abstract Noun Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: Can it not be seen or touched? Step 2: Is it a feeling or quality? Then it's an Abstract Noun.
tricks.example: Honesty is the best policy. 'honesty' is an Abstract Noun.

tricks.title: Question Method Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: Ask a question before the word – Who? What? How? Step 2: Determine the category according to the answer.
tricks.example: He spoke loudly. How did he speak? 'loudly' – Adverb.

tricks.title: Comparison Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: If it has -er or -est attached, it will often be an Adjective. Step 2: Check whether it shows a comparison or not.
tricks.example: Ravi is taller than Aman. 'taller' is an Adjective.
